name: What is the difference between wood and metal stud framing for remodels?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between wood and metal stud framing for remodels?

acceptedAnswer.text: Wood framing uses standard dimensional lumber (usually 2x4s or 2x6s), while metal framing uses lightweight galvanized steel studs. Wood is the standard choice for residential remodeling because it easily supports heavy cabinets, solid doors, wall-mounted TVs, and complex trim carpentry. Metal studs are completely straight, rot-resistant, and non-combustible, but they require specialized fasteners and wood blocking if you plan to hang heavy fixtures. For most residential kitchen, bath, and basement remodels, wood framing provides the necessary backing and versatility for finish carpentry and drywall fastening.
acceptedAnswer.description: Wood framing offers superior support for heavy cabinetry and trim, whereas steel framing resists moisture and stays straight but requires extra blocking for heavy items.
